source_text: Ταῦτα δὲ οὐ μόνον πρὸς τὰ ἐκκείμενα περὶ τῶν ἐποπτῶν ἡμῖν λέλεκται, ἀλλὰ καὶ μετρίως προλαμβάνουσι τὰ ὑπὸ τοῦ Κέλσου πρὸς ἡμᾶς λεγόμενα. ἐν οἷς φησιν· ἴτω δὲ ὁ δεύτερος· ἐρήσομαι δὲ αὐτοὺς, πόθεν ἥκουσιν ἢ τίνα ἔχουσιν ἀρχηγέτην πατρίων νόμων. οὐδένα φήσουσιν, οἵ γε ἐκεῖθεν μὲν ὥρμηνται καὶ αὐτοὶ καὶ τὸν διδάσκαλόν τε καὶ χοροστάτην οὐκ ἄλλοθέν ποθεν φέρουσιν· ὅμως δ᾿ ἀφεστήκασιν Ἰουδαίων. ἥκομεν οὖν ἡμεῖς ἕκαστος „ἐν ταῖς ἐσχάταις ἡμέραις,“ ὅτε ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἡμῶν ἐπιδεδήμηκεν, εἰς „τὸ ἐμφανὲς ὄρος κυρίου,“ τὸν „ὑπεράνω“ παντὸς λόγου λόγον, καὶ εἰς τὸν οἶκον „τοῦ θεοῦ.“ ὅς „ἐστιν ἐκκλησία θεοῦ ζῶντος, στῦλος καὶ ἑδραίωμα τῆς ἀληθείας.“ καὶ ὁρῶμεν τίνα τρόπον οὗτος οἰκοδομεῖται „ἐπὶ ἄκρων τῶν ὀρέων,“ πάντων τῶν προφητικῶν λόγων, οἵτινες αὐτοῦ θεμέλιός εἰσιν. ὑψοῦται δ᾿ οὗτος „ὁ οἶκος“ „ὑπεράνω τῶν βουνῶν,“ τῶν δοκούντων τι ἐξαίρετον παρὰ ἀνθρώποις ἐν σοφίᾳ καὶ ἀληθείᾳ ἐπαγγέλλεσθαι. καὶ ἐρχόμεθα „πάντα τὰ ἔθνη“ ἐπ᾿ αὐτὸ, καὶ πορευόμεθα τὰ πολλὰ ἔθνη, καὶ λέγομεν ἀλλήλοις, προτρέποντες ἐπὶ τὴν „ἐν ἐσχάταις ἡμέραις“ ἀναλάμψασαν διὰ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ θεοσέβειαν· „δεῦτε καὶ ἀναβῶμεν εἰς τὸ ὄρος τοῦ κυρίου καὶ εἰς τὸν οἶκον τοῦ θεοῦ Ἰακὼβ. καὶ ἀναγγελεῖ ἡμῖν τὴν ὁδὸν αὐτοῦ, καὶ πορευσόμεθα ἐν αὐτῇ.“ ἐξῆλθε γὰρ ἀπὸ τῶν ἐν „Σιὼν“ „νόμος“ καὶ μετέστη ἐφ᾿ ἡμᾶς πνευματικός. ἀλλὰ καὶ „ὁ λόγος κυρίου“ ἐξῆλθεν ἀπ᾿ ἐκείνης τῆς „Ἱερουσαλὴμ,“ ἵνα πανταχοῦ νεμηθῇ καὶ κρίνῃ „ἀνὰ μέσον τῶν ἐθνῶν,“ ἐκλεγόμενος μὲν οὓς ὁρᾷ εὐπειθεῖς ἐλέγχῃ δὲ „λαὸν πολὺν“ τὸν ἀπειθῆ. καί φαμεν γὲ πρὸς τοὺς ἐρομένους ἡμᾶς, πόθεν ἥκομεν ἢ τίνα ἔχομεν ἀρχηγέτην, ὅτι ἤλθομεν κατὰ τὰς Ἰησοῦ ὑποθήκας συγκόψαι „τὰς“ πολεμικὰς ἡμῶν λογικὰς „μαχαίρας“ καὶ ὑβριστικὰς „εἰς ἄροτρα,“ καὶ „τὰς“ κατὰ τὸ πρότερον ἡμῶν μάχιμον „ζιβύνας εἰς δρέπανα“ μετασκευάζομεν. οὐκέτι γὰρ λαμβάνομεν „ἐπ᾿ ἔθνος μάχαιραν“ οὐδὲ μανθάνομεν „ἔτι πολεμεῖν,“ γενόμενοι διὰ τὸν Ἰησοῦν υἱοὶ τῆς εἰρήνης, ὅς ἐστιν ἡμῶν ἀρχηγὸς, ἀντὶ τῶν πατρίων, ἐν οἷς „ξένοι τῶν διαθηκῶν“ ἐτυγχάνομεν, λαμβάνοντες νόμον, ἐφ᾿ ᾧ χάριτας ὁμολογοῦντες τῷ ἡμᾶς ῥυσαμένῳ ἀπὸ τῆς πλάνης λέγομεν· „ὡς ψευδῆ ἐκτήσαντο οἱ πατέρες ἡμῶν εἴδωλα, καὶ οὐκ ἔστιν ἐν αὐτοῖς ὑετίζων.“ ὁ χοροστάτης οὖν ἡμῶν καὶ διδάσκαλος ἀπὸ Ἰουδαίων ἐξελθὼν ὅλην νέμεται τῷ λόγῳ τῆς διδασκαλίας, ἑαυτοῦ τὴν οἰκουμένην. καὶ ταῦτα μὲν προλαβόντες πολλοῖς ἐπιφερομένην τοῦ Κέλσου λέξιν ὅση δύναμις ἀνετρέψαμεν, συνάπτοντες τοῖς ἐκκειμένοις αὐτοῦ ῥητοῖς.
pass_a_gloss: These things have been said by us not only against what was set out (ἐκκείμενα) about the overseers (ἐπόπται), but they also moderately (μετρίως) anticipate (προλαμβάνω) the things said by Celsus against us. In which he says: 'Let the second (ὁ δεύτερος) come; I will ask them whence they come, or whom they have as founder (ἀρχηγέτης) of ancestral laws (πάτριοι νόμοι). They will say none (οὐδένα), they who themselves have set out (ὁρμάομαι) from there and bring the teacher and chorus leader (χοροστάτης) from nowhere else; yet they have revolted (ἀφίστημι) from the Jews.' We then have come, each, 'in the last days', when our Jesus has sojourned (ἐπιδημέω), to 'the manifest (ἐμφανής) mountain of the Lord', the Word 'above' every word, and to the house 'of God', which 'is the church of the living God, pillar (στῦλος) and foundation (ἑδραίωμα) of the truth'. And we see in what way this is built 'on the tops of the mountains', all the prophetic words, which are its foundation (θεμέλιος). And this 'house' is raised (ὑψόω) 'above the hills', those seeming to profess (ἐπαγγέλλομαι) something exceptional (ἐξαίρετον) among men in wisdom and truth. And we come, 'all the nations', to it, and we go, the many nations, and say to one another, urging (προτρέπω) toward the godliness (θεοσέβεια) that shone forth (ἀναλάμπω) 'in the last days' through Jesus Christ: 'Come and let us go up to the mountain of the Lord and to the house of the God of Jacob, and he will announce (ἀναγγέλλω) to us his way, and we will walk in it.' For 'law' went out from those in 'Zion' and passed over (μεθίστημι) to us as spiritual (πνευματικός). But also 'the word of the Lord' went out from that 'Jerusalem', so that it might be distributed (νέμω) everywhere and judge 'between the nations', choosing those he sees obedient (εὐπειθής), and reproving (ἐλέγχω) the disobedient (ἀπειθής) 'many people'. And we say to those asking us whence we come or whom we have as founder, that we have come according to the counsels (ὑποθῆκαι) of Jesus to cut down (συγκόπτω) our warlike rational (λογικός) and insolent (ὑβριστικός) 'swords into ploughs', and 'the spears' (ζιβύνη) of our former fighting we refashion (μετασκευάζω) 'into sickles'. For we no longer take 'sword against nation' nor learn 'any more to make war', having become through Jesus sons of peace (υἱοὶ τῆς εἰρήνης), who is our founder (ἀρχηγός), instead of the ancestral things, in which we happened to be 'strangers of the covenants (ξένοι τῶν διαθηκῶν)', receiving a law, for which confessing thanks to the one who rescued (ῥύομαι) us from error (πλάνη) we say: 'How false (ψευδῆ) idols our fathers acquired, and there is not among them one sending rain (ὑετίζων).' Our chorus leader and teacher, then, having come out from the Jews, holds (νέμομαι) by the word of teaching the whole inhabited world (οἰκουμένη) as his own. And anticipating (προλαμβάνω) these things, we have overturned (ἀνατρέπω) as far as possible a passage (λέξις) of Celsus coming many (sections) later, joining it to his statements (ῥητά) set out.

pass_b_english: What we have said was said not only in answer to what was set out about the overseers; it also in some measure anticipates what Celsus says against us. For he says: “Let the second party come forward. I will ask them where they have come from, or whom they have as the founder of their ancestral laws. They will name no one, since they themselves set out from there and bring their teacher and chorus leader from nowhere else; and yet they have broken away from the Jews.”

We, then, have come, each of us, “in the last days,” when our Jesus has come to visit us, to “the manifest mountain of the Lord” (Isaiah 2:2), that is, to the Word who is “above” every word, and to the house “of God,” which “is the church of the living God, the pillar and foundation of the truth” (1 Timothy 3:15). And we see in what way this house is built “on the tops of the mountains,” that is, on all the prophetic words, which are its foundation. And this “house” is raised “above the hills” (Isaiah 2:2), that is, above those who appear to profess something exceptional among men in wisdom and truth.

And we, “all the nations,” come to it, and we, the many nations, go, and say to one another, as we urge each other on toward the worship of God that shone out “in the last days” through Jesus Christ: “Come, let us go up to the mountain of the Lord and to the house of the God of Jacob, and he will declare his way to us, and we will walk in it” (Isaiah 2:2–3). For the “law” went out from those in “Zion” and passed over to us as a spiritual law (Isaiah 2:3). And “the word of the Lord” also went out from that “Jerusalem” (Isaiah 2:3), so that it might spread everywhere and judge “between the nations,” choosing those whom he sees are ready to obey, and reproving the “many people” who will not obey (Isaiah 2:4).

And to those who ask us where we have come from, or whom we have as our founder, we say that we have come, following the counsels of Jesus, to beat our warlike and insolent “swords” of speech “into ploughshares,” and we are refashioning “the spears” of our former fighting “into sickles” (Isaiah 2:4). For we no longer take up “sword against nation,” nor do we learn “to make war any more” (Isaiah 2:4), since because of Jesus we have become sons of peace. He is our founder; and in place of the ancestral laws, under which we were “strangers to the covenants” (Ephesians 2:12), we have received a law, for which we give thanks to him who rescued us from error, and say: “How false were the idols our fathers acquired, and there is none among them that sends rain” (Jeremiah 16:19; 14:22).

So our chorus leader and teacher, having gone out from the Jews, holds the whole inhabited world as his own by the word of his teaching. In saying this in advance, we have overturned, as far as we could, a passage of Celsus that comes much later, joining it to his statements already set out.
notes: Celsus's words (ἴτω δὲ ὁ δεύτερος ... ἀφεστήκασιν Ἰουδαίων) are quoted from a later place in his book, as Origen says at the end of the chapter; set in quotation marks. 'The second party' (ὁ δεύτερος): Celsus has dealt with the Jews and now calls on the Christians; the masculine may imply 'second chorus', matching χοροστάτης, but the noun is not expressed. ἀρχηγέτης (Celsus) and ἀρχηγός (Origen, of Jesus) both rendered 'founder' to keep Origen's answer to Celsus's question visible; ἀρχηγός can also mean 'author' or 'leader' (compare Acts 3:15; Hebrews 2:10; 12:2; not cited). The chapter is built on Isaiah 2:2-4 LXX (parallel Micah 4:1-3), quoted in pieces and glossed: 'manifest mountain', 'on the tops of the mountains', 'above the hills', 'all the nations', 'many nations', 'Come, let us go up ...', 'law from Zion, word of the Lord from Jerusalem', 'judge between the nations, reprove many people', swords into ploughshares and spears (ζιβύνη) into sickles, no more sword against nation or learning war. Origen's interpretive glosses (the Word above every word; the prophetic words as foundation; the hills as those claiming wisdom; the law passing to us as spiritual) are kept as his. 1 Timothy 3:15 quoted exactly. 'Strangers to the covenants' is Ephesians 2:12. The closing prayer joins Jeremiah 16:19 LXX ('how false were the idols our fathers acquired', where the LXX ends 'and there is no profit in them') with Jeremiah 14:22 LXX ('is there among the idols of the nations one that sends rain?'). λογικὰς μαχαίρας ('rational/verbal swords') is doubtful: rendered 'swords of speech', meaning the hostile words of the former pagan life; Origen may mean that Christians once fought with words. Possible allusions not cited inline: 'children of peace' (Luke 10:6, 'son of peace'); 'the law ... spiritual' (Romans 7:14); 'prophetic words, which are its foundation' (Ephesians 2:20). νέμεται / νεμηθῇ continue the allotment theme of 5.25-32 (the Word now holds the whole world as his portion); rendered 'holds ... as his own' and 'spread'. The staged text punctuates 'θεοῦ. ὅς' and ἡμῶν, ἑαυτοῦ oddly; read as continuous sentences. ἀντὶ τῶν πατρίων is taken with λαμβάνοντες νόμον ('in place of the ancestral laws ... we have received a law'), answering Celsus's question about the founder of 'ancestral laws' (πατρίων νόμων). γενόμενοι διὰ τὸν Ἰησοῦν (accusative) rendered 'because of Jesus', not 'through'.

Open doubt (review): 5.33: λογικὰς μαχαίρας is still rendered 'swords of speech'. The sense ('rational' or 'verbal' swords) is unsure, and the translator's note flags it. I judged it acceptable and passed the chapter, but the owner may want a second view.
